slides.heading: Plea of a Bruised Soul
bullet_points: A poem by Tarun Gupta
About being witnessed — not fixed
slides.speaker_note: Open with the title and set a single expectation: this is about a specific kind of loneliness, not pain in general.

slides.heading: The wrong kind of comfort
bullet_points: It rushes in before the wound has finished bleeding
It reframes. It offers silver linings. It hands you cement.
The person learns to stop saying how they really feel.
slides.speaker_note: Name the familiar pattern before the poem — earn recognition before asking for vulnerability.

slides.heading: Don't ask me to be stronger
bullet_points: I am already holding what I cannot name.
Don't tell me time will mend this —
time is how I measured the breaking.
slides.speaker_note: Read slowly — let the lines land as poetry, not as information.

slides.heading: I don't need your silver linings
bullet_points: or the map to somewhere better.
I need you to sit with me
in this room where the ceiling has caved.
slides.speaker_note: This is the emotional center — pause after 'caved' before moving on.

slides.heading: Witness vs Rescue
bullet_points: Witness: I see this is real. I am not leaving.
Rescue: Let me make this something else so we can both feel better sooner.
One stays. The other implies you should be somewhere else by now.
slides.speaker_note: The core distinction of the whole piece — give it its own slide, don't rush past it.

slides.heading: Just stay.
bullet_points: Stay like weather.
Stay like the dark before dawn
that doesn't promise anything — just holds you until morning decides to come.
slides.speaker_note: Let 'stay like weather' breathe — it's the most unexpected image and the one people remember.

slides.heading: The whole ask
bullet_points: I am not asking for rescue.
I am asking to be witnessed.
See me here, exactly as I am, and don't look away.
slides.speaker_note: End on the poem's close — no commentary on this slide, let the lines finish the room.
